main_text.p: Princeps, inq; cuius tutelam atq; patro-cinium illum committerem, inveni ne-minem. Merito enim Germaniæ no-strę ecclesiæ orthodoxæ gratis animis agnoscunt atque prædicant insigne hoc Dei beneficiū, merito, inquam, sibi gau-dent, quòd in turbulento hoc, confuso & ancipiti nouissimorum horum temporū statu, Tuam Cels. excitavit, iisq; ingenii, animi & corporis dotibus, eâ in omni li-teraturæ genere eruditione varia, exqui-sita & rara, eâ sapientiâ atque prudentiâ, eâ justitiâ, æquitate, clementiâ, humani-tate, beneficentiâ, magnanimitate, tem-perantiâ, sobrietate, & laborum toleran-tiâ donavit, ut vera & expressa naturę bo-ni Principis imago in illa exstet, præcla-ramq; adeo magis, & ecclesiæ afflictæ, & patriæ atque reipublicæ nutanti operam navare; veritatem plurimorum odiis, ca-lumniis & persecutionibus obnoxiam, fortiter asserere, vindicare & propagare, columnaque in domo Dei viventis infi-gnis esse queat. Quemadmodum mul-torum piorum & bonorum oculi hic in te Illustrissime & Magnanime Princeps, conjecti sunt, qui magnas de Cels. Tuâ spes intra animos suos conceperunt, il-

page.notes: Right edge: a strip of the facing page is cut off by the gutter and not transcribed. Uncertain readings: "strę" and "nostrę" near the line start are read from a partly hidden word; "orthodoxæ" and "Germaniæ" are clear. The catchword "lamq;" is set at the lower right and completes the hyphenated "il-" at the line end. No page number is printed on this page.
